source_rows.literal: * The combat logging mechanism is completely overhauled with explicit data instead of text strings delivered to the UI. Highlights include detailed flags indicating relationship of involved units to player, unique identifiers for units with the same name within the combat log -- great for log analysis.<ref>{{Ref web|url=http://forums.worldofwarcraft.com/thread.html?topicId=2968233433&pageNo=1&sid=1#9|date=20071119|archivedate=20071119|archiveurl=http://blue.cardplace.com/newcache/us/2968233433.htm|title=Upcoming 2.4 API changes - concise list}}</ref>
source_rows.note: UNPROVEN: combat logging changes from text strings to explicit data, relationship flags and unique same-name unit identifiers. Actual event payload schema and GUID-format/transport proof absent; cited forum not expanded.

source_rows.literal: ** [[Patch_2.4.0/Consolidated API changes/Guide to the New Combat Log|Guide to the New Combat Log]]

source_rows.literal: * The In-game Interface Options screen is being revamped and the new architecture should allow AddOn authors to modify its contents without the taint issues presented by the current system. Additionally this system will contain an area for AddOn authors to present their own configuration options. Authors interested in this feature should be sure to experiment on the PTRs before patch 2.4 is released so that any issues can be surfaced and discussed. Basic details on how to use this system can be found in code comments in the 2.4 UIOptionsPanels.lua.
source_rows.note: UNPROVEN: addon Interface Options extension and taint issues require actual panel integration/security proof; future PTR experiment and UIOptionsPanels.lua comments are not supplied evidence.

source_rows.literal: * NEW - [[bagType]] = [[API GetItemFamily|GetItemFamily]](itemId or itemName or itemLink or itemString) -- When used with a container, this returns the type of container. signature_rows.literal: * NEW - [[bagType]] = [[API GetItemFamily|GetItemFamily]](itemId or itemName or itemLink or itemString) -- When used with a container, this returns the type of container. When used with an item, it returns the type of container the item can go in. However, [[bagType]] is a bitflag, so [[API GetItemFamily|GetItemFamily]] for something that could go in a quiver ([[bagType]] 1) and an ammo pouch ([[bagType]] 2) would return 3. A bag that can hold both arrows and bullets would also return 3.
signature_rows.note: UNPROVEN: GetItemFamily returns item/container eligibility bits; quiver 1 OR ammo pouch 2 equals 3, for items or combined-capacity bags. Exact bit catalog follows; no modern equivalence assumed. Literal call fragment retained; result/validation/lifecycle not established by spelling.
